A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–D. The supplement's relocation behind the references in v2 does not create evidence gaps.

before.justification: V1 reports original pose-estimation experiments on four datasets, together with ablations, synthetic depth-shift tests, and qualitative results.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds evaluated scale-only solver comparisons, including supplementary Tables 9–10.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4 retain the affine-depth formulation, three proposed solvers, and hybrid LO-MSAC procedure. The runtime parameter tuning does not introduce a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: ScanNet-1500, MegaDepth-1500, ETH3D, and Stanford 2D-3D-S remain, with the same calibration tasks, covisibility evaluation, and synthetic-shift scenario. Removing some matcher configurations does not change dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 substantially expands calibrated comparisons with Barath and Sweeney [4]: 2PT+D & 4PT+D, 2PT+D & 5pt, and Simulated P3P & 5pt. These previously unevaluated scale-only configurations appear in new Tables 9–10, with selected comparisons also added to Tables 1–2.

E3.justification: Tables 1 and 3 drop SP+SG configurations, although SP+SG remains in ablations. Runtime evaluation changes from four local-optimization steps and at least 1,000 iterations to unspecified tuned LO/RANSAC settings. Dataset construction, image resolutions, and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The shift and hybrid-component ablations, covisibility analysis, synthetic-shift tests, MDE-model comparison, and qualitative cases are retained. New Tables 9–10 provide baseline comparisons rather than new ablation or robustness analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Reporting remains based on median errors and AUC values.

E6.justification: V2 adds a substantial body of calibrated results against three scale-only configurations, removes SP+SG main-table blocks, and revises selected existing scores. For example, Table 2's DA-met. AUC at 5 degrees changes from 57.93 to 59.80. Runtime medians change from 360/610/950 ms to 31/65/129 ms under tuned settings, preventing a direct same-setting speed comparison.

T1.justification: Equations 1–10, solver derivations and solution counts, and Appendix C's minimality reasoning and alternative elimination-template discussion remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims about affine corrections, three calibration-specific solvers, hybrid estimation, and compatibility with different matchers and depth models. Added comparisons support these existing claims.

C2.justification: The explanations of affine corrections, unreliable depth, and limited covisibility remain, as do Appendix D's limitations. The new baseline discussion reiterates the existing scale-only and rank-deficiency arguments.

D1.justification: V2 specifies author-supplied baseline implementations within GC-RANSAC and clarifies that DUSt3R/MASt3R use direct pointmaps without global alignment. Conversely, runtime reporting loses explicit LO/iteration counts and the single-thread qualification. Code access and core implementation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Both versions cite the same 82 works and retain Section 2's research positioning. The new comparisons test an already stated distinction from scale-only methods. Updates to publication venues are bibliographic changes.

P1.justification: Baseline and runtime paragraphs receive limited rewriting. References move before the renamed Supplementary Material, acknowledgements move into the main text, and the MDE-applicability paragraph moves to supplementary Section B. Most prose and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables 9–10, changes the row structure of Tables 1–3, condenses several captions, and relocates supplementary pages. Figures 1–9 retain the same visual evidence, and the overall layout remains similar.

improvement.justification: Direct comparisons with closely related scale-only solvers strengthen evidence for affine corrections, and baseline implementation disclosures improve clarity. These focused gains are tempered by less reproducible runtime reporting and an unexplained inconsistency: updated MegaDepth MoGe results in Table 2 no longer match the retained full-model row in Table 6.
